# Family-based cross-provider failover

> **Priority**: P3 — extends the existing router failover (which already retries *within* a set) to switch **across providers** when the same model family is available elsewhere. Builds on the daemon; doesn't affect CLI ping.
> **Inspiration**: `apmantza/pi-free` — `lib/model-detection.ts` (family mapping) + their `provider-failover/` directory.
> **Cross-surface**: daemon-side; transparent to all client surfaces.

---

## 1. Why

The FCM Router (per `tasks/PRD-smart-model-router.md`) already does failover **within a set**: if `nvidiaNim/deepseek-v4-pro` 429s, it tries the next model *in the set list*. But the next entry might be a totally different family (Qwen, Llama) — the user asked for DeepSeek-class output and gets a behaviour change mid-conversation.

pi-free's `lib/model-detection.ts` normalizes every model to a **family** (`claude`, `deepseek`, `gemini`, `gpt`, `llama`, `minimax`, `qwen`, `nemotron`, `kimi`, `glm`, `mistral`, `arcee`, `openai-o`). Combined with their failover dir, they can reroute `OpenRouter/deepseek-v4` → `Cerebras/deepseek-v4` → `Together/deepseek-v3` keeping the user in the DeepSeek family.

This task makes the router prefer **family-preserving** failover: when a model fails, look for the same family on another provider before falling back to a different family.

---

## 2. Goals / Non-goals

### Goals
- [ ] Normalize every model in our merged list to a `family` id (12 families, mirror pi-free's `BRAND_MAPPINGS`).
- [ ] When a routed request fails, prefer retrying on a healthy model of the **same family** at a different provider.
- [ ] Fall back to the existing set-order failover when no same-family alternative exists.
- [ ] Surface the failover decision in `/stream/events` (already emits `request` events) and the Router Dashboard TUI.
- [ ] Configurable: per-set toggle `familyFailover: true|false`.

### Non-goals
- Family detection for ping (we only need it at routing time).
- Cross-family "equivalence" scoring (e.g. treating Qwen as DeepSeek-equivalent) — explicit family match only.
- Replacing the circuit breaker (it still gates each (provider,model) pair).

---

## 3. Technical design

### 3.1 Family detection: `src/core/model-family.js`

Port pi-free's `BRAND_MAPPINGS`:

```js
const BRAND_MAPPINGS = [
  { keywords: ['claude'],          familyId: 'claude',   familyName: 'Claude' },
  { keywords: ['deepseek'],        familyId: 'deepseek', familyName: 'DeepSeek' },
  { keywords: ['gemini'],          familyId: 'gemini',   familyName: 'Gemini' },
  { keywords: ['gpt'],             familyId: 'gpt',      familyName: 'GPT' },
  { keywords: ['llama'],           familyId: 'llama',    familyName: 'Llama' },
  { keywords: ['minimax'],         familyId: 'minimax',  familyName: 'MiniMax' },
  { keywords: ['qwen'],            familyId: 'qwen',     familyName: 'Qwen' },
  { keywords: ['nemotron'],        familyId: 'nemotron', familyName: 'Nemotron' },
  { keywords: ['kimi','moonshot'], familyId: 'kimi',     familyName: 'Kimi' },
  { keywords: ['glm','chatglm'],   familyId: 'glm',      familyName: 'GLM' },
  { keywords: ['mistral'],         familyId: 'mistral',  familyName: 'Mistral' },
  { keywords: ['o1','o3'],         familyId: 'openai-o', familyName: 'OpenAI o' },
];

export function detectFamily(model) {
  const haystack = [model.id, model.label, model.providerKey]
    .filter(Boolean).join(' ').toLowerCase();
  for (const m of BRAND_MAPPINGS) {
    if (m.keywords.some(k => haystack.includes(k))) return m.familyId;
  }
  return null;
}
```

### 3.2 Family index build (at set-activation time)

```js
// when a set is activated, build:
//   familyIndex: Map<familyId, Array<{ providerKey, modelId, healthy }>>
// sorted by (healthy desc, latency asc)
```

### 3.3 Failover policy change (in `router-daemon.js`)

Today (per PRD): failover iterates the set list top-down. Change to two-stage:

```js
function pickNextModel(failedModel, set, circuitBreaker) {
  // Stage 1: same family, healthy, different provider
  const family = detectFamily(failedModel);
  if (family && set.familyFailover !== false) {
    const sameFamily = set.familyIndex.get(family) ?? [];
    const candidate = sameFamily.find(c =>
      c.providerKey !== failedModel.providerKey &&
      circuitBreaker.isOpen(c.providerKey, c.modelId) === false
    );
    if (candidate) return { ...candidate, reason: 'family_failover' };
  }
  // Stage 2: existing set-order fallback
  return set.nextInOrder(failedModel) ?? null;
}
```

### 3.4 Observability

- `/stream/events` `request` event gains a `failoverReason: 'family_failover' | 'set_order' | 'none'`.
- Router Dashboard TUI request log shows the family hop (e.g. `nvidiaNim/deepseek-v4-pro → together/deepseek-v3  [family]`).
- Telemetry: `router_family_failover` event (sampled).

---

## 4. Subtasks

- [x] **4.1** Create `src/core/model-family.js` (`detectFamily`, `BRAND_MAPPINGS`).
- [x] **4.2** Build `familyIndex` at set activation (extend set schema in `src/core/router-daemon.js`). *(adapted: families are computed on demand from the live routing candidates via `detectFamily` instead of a cached index - always fresh, no invalidation logic, same O(n) cost)*
- [x] **4.3** Implement `pickNextModel` two-stage policy. *(pure `pickNextCandidate` in model-family.js; routeRequest swaps the picked candidate into the attempt chain)*
- [x] **4.4** Add `familyFailover: true|false` to set schema (default `true`).
- [x] **4.5** Expose `failoverReason` in `/stream/events` + render in Router Dashboard TUI. *(requestLog entries carry `failover_reason`; TUI + Web dashboards render the `family` tag)*
- [x] **4.6** Telemetry event `router_family_failover`. *(adapted: existing `app_router_failover` event gained a `failover_reason` property instead of a new event)*
- [x] **4.7** Tests:
  - `test/model-family.test.js` — each family detected; case-insensitive; unknown returns null; `o1`/`o3` don't false-positive on `gpt-oss`. *(21 unit tests)*
  - Integration tests live in `test/test.js` (router suite): failing `nvidia/gpt-oss-120b` hops to `cerebras/gpt-oss-120b` and skips the Qwen entry; `familyFailover:false` reverts to set-order. *(2 tests)*
- [x] **4.8** Set Manager TUI (`Shift+S`): show a family toggle. *(adapted: no Set Manager TUI screen exists; the toggle is a "Family failover" button on the Web Router Dashboard set panel, settable via `PUT /sets/:name`)*
- [x] **4.9** Docs: explain family-preserving failover + the toggle. *(README router section + TUI help screen)*
- [x] **4.10** Changelog entry. (`changelog/v0.5.82.md`, version to confirm at bump time)

---

## 5. Acceptance criteria

- [x] When `nvidiaNim/deepseek-v4-pro` fails and `together/deepseek-v3` is healthy in the set, the router hops to Together first (not to a Qwen entry above it). *(integration test: failing `nvidia/gpt-oss-120b` → `cerebras/gpt-oss-120b`, Qwen entry never called)*
- [x] With `familyFailover:false`, behaviour matches today (set-order). *(integration test: Qwen at priority 2 gets served)*
- [x] Router Dashboard visibly tags family hops `[family]`. *(TUI + Web request logs render `family` in the detail column)*
- [x] `pnpm test` green (target ≥74 tests). *(836 tests / 162 suites, 0 fail; baseline was 813)*
- [x] No regression on the existing failover tests (auth errors, streaming, all-down 503, etc.). *(full suite green)*

---

## 8. Worklog & evidence (2026-09-05, agent zcode)

- **Branch**: `feat/t8-family-failover` in worktree `../free-coding-models-t8-family-failover`, based on `origin/main` (f611aae). Commit `32f3262`.
- **New module** `src/core/model-family.js`: ordered `BRAND_MAPPINGS` (12 families; `gpt` before `openai-o`, `nemotron` before `llama`), `detectFamily` over a lowercased id+label+provider haystack, word-boundary matching for `o1`/`o3`, pure `pickNextCandidate({ candidates, failedCandidate, triedKeys, blockedProviders, familyFailover })` returning `{ candidate, reason: 'family_failover'|'set_order' }`.
- **Daemon** (`src/core/router-daemon.js`): the failover loop keeps an `attemptChain` copy; after `pickNextCandidate` a family pick is spliced in as the next attempt (without this reorder the pick was cosmetic - caught by the integration test). `addRequestLog` merges `failover_reason` from the active request so requestLog, `/stats`, and the SSE `request` event all expose it. `app_router_failover` telemetry gains `failover_reason`; warn log gets a `[family]` suffix.
- **Config** (`src/core/config.js`): `normalizeRouterSets` keeps `familyFailover` per set (default true), so it round-trips through `PUT /sets/:name` and survives restarts.
- **UI**: TUI Router Dashboard + Web `RouterView.jsx` render `family` instead of `failover` for family hops; Web set panel gets a "Family failover: on/off" button.
- **Verification evidence**:
  - `pnpm test`: 836 tests / 162 suites / 0 fail (baseline before change: 813 / 0 fail).
  - `pnpm build:web` succeeds with the new JSX (web dist rebuilt in the worktree).
  - `free-coding-models --help` renders the new failover text; TUI boots and Shift+R dashboard opens without crash (tmux session, cleaned up after).
  - Unit: `node --test test/model-family.test.js` → 21/21. Integration: family hop + toggle-off tests green.
- **Env note**: worktrees need `mkdir -p packages/node_modules && ln -s ../.. packages/node_modules/free-coding-models` (self-link for `packages/fcm-agent-core`, gitignored, exists only in the main checkout) and `pnpm build:web` (web/dist is gitignored), otherwise 2 environment-dependent tests fail.

---

## 6. Risks & mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Family detection false positives (`o1` matching inside `gpt-oss-120b`'s id? — check: `gpt` matches first, so fine; but `o1` keyword must be word-boundary-checked) | Order `BRAND_MAPPINGS` so `gpt` precedes `openai-o`; add tests for the tricky ids in `sources.js`. |
| Family hop hides a provider outage from the user | Surface it loudly in the dashboard + telemetry; don't silently swallow. |
| User wants strict set order | `familyFailover:false` per set; default `true` but documented. |
| Different providers expose different context windows for the "same" family | Acceptable — failover is best-effort; the alternative (conversation-breaking family switch) is worse. |

---

## 7. References

- pi-free `lib/model-detection.ts` — `BRAND_MAPPINGS`, `PROVIDER_MAPPINGS`, family normalization.
- pi-free `provider-failover/` directory — their failover subsystem (benchmark-aware).
- Our `tasks/PRD-smart-model-router.md` §2.1 "Request failover ✅ Backend done" — the existing within-set failover to extend.
- Our `src/core/router-daemon.js` — integration point.
- Our Router Dashboard TUI (per PRD, `Shift+R`) — observability surface.

# Passive quota monitoring via response headers

> **Priority**: P1 — eliminates wasted quota-fetch requests and keeps quota *live* during real usage.
> **Inspiration**: `apmantza/pi-free` — `lib/quota-monitor.ts` (which itself credits us: *"Inspired by free-coding-models' extractQuotaPercent"*).
> **Cross-surface**: shared `src/core/provider-quota-fetchers.js` is consumed by CLI, daemon, and Tauri.

---

## 1. Why

Today we discover a provider's remaining quota by **actively fetching** a dedicated quota endpoint (see `src/core/provider-quota-fetchers.js` + `test/provider-quota-fetchers.test.js`). Problems:

- **Extra requests** that consume the very quota we're trying to measure (SambaNova per-minute windows, Groq daily caps).
- **Not all providers expose a quota endpoint** — for those we currently show nothing.
- **Stale between polls** — the daemon polls every N seconds; between polls the displayed `%` is wrong, so users get rate-limited mid-request.

pi-free's insight: **every chat-completion response already carries rate-limit headers**. By hooking the response pipeline (they use Pi's `after_provider_response` event) and parsing 5 header variants in priority order, they get a *free, always-fresh* quota signal with **zero extra requests**.

We should do the same on **two** of our surfaces:

1. **Daemon reverse-proxy** (`src/core/router-daemon.js`) — every routed request's response passes through us; we parse the headers there.
2. **Ping responses** (`src/core/ping.js`) — even health-check pings return headers; we can pre-warm quota before the user ever routes.

The active `provider-quota-fetchers.js` stays as a **fallback** for providers that don't emit headers (e.g. some that need an explicit `/usage` call).

---

## 2. Goals / Non-goals

### Goals
- [ ] Parse rate-limit headers from **every** response that flows through the daemon and through pings.
- [ ] Support the 5 header-pair variants pi-free supports (see 3.2) **plus** any we already handle.
- [ ] Merge with existing active-fetch quota so the displayed value is the freshest of the two.
- [ ] Mark quota as **stale after 5 min** (no header seen recently → fall back to active fetch or hide the chip).
- [ ] Expose via `/stats` and the TUI footer so the user sees live `%` per provider.
- [ ] Zero extra network requests compared to today.

### Non-goals
- Replacing `provider-quota-fetchers.js` entirely (keep as fallback).
- Per-model quota (we track per-provider, since headers are per-provider-key).
- Quota-based auto-routing decisions (separate task; this is observability only).

---

## 3. Technical design

### 3.1 Module: extend `src/core/provider-quota-fetchers.js`

Add a passive tracker alongside the existing active fetchers:

```js
// in-memory quota state (mirrors pi-free's _quotaState Map)
const _passiveQuota = new Map(); // providerKey -> QuotaSnapshot

export function processResponseHeaders(providerKey, headers) {
  const extracted = extractQuota(headers);
  if (!extracted) return;
  _passiveQuota.set(providerKey, { ...extracted, percent, lastUpdated: Date.now() });
}

export function getQuota(providerKey) { /* merge passive + active, return freshest */ }
export function getAllQuotas() { /* ReadonlyMap for /stats */ }
export function formatQuotaStatus(providerKey) { /* "⚠️ groq: 12/100 (12%)" */ }
```

### 3.2 Header-pair variants (priority order)

Straight from pi-free's `HEADER_PAIRS`, each pair is `[remaining, limit]`:

```js
const HEADER_PAIRS = [
  // Per-minute (most common)
  ['x-ratelimit-remaining-requests', 'x-ratelimit-limit-requests'], // SambaNova
  ['x-ratelimit-remaining',          'x-ratelimit-limit'],          // Mistral
  ['ratelimit-remaining-requests',   'ratelimit-limit-requests'],
  ['ratelimit-remaining',            'ratelimit-limit'],
  // Per-day
  ['x-ratelimit-remaining-requests-day', 'x-ratelimit-limit-requests-day'], // SambaNova daily
  ['x-ratelimit-remaining-day',          'x-ratelimit-limit-day'],
];
```

**Case-insensitive**: normalize all header keys to lowercase before matching (some proxies vary casing). Return the **first** pair where both `remaining` and `limit` parse as finite numbers and `limit > 0`.

### 3.3 Integration points

#### 3.3.1 Daemon reverse proxy (`src/core/router-daemon.js`)

The daemon already proxies `/v1/chat/completions`. In the response handler (after we forward headers, before we stream the body to the client), call:

```js
processResponseHeaders(upstreamProviderKey, upstreamResponse.headers);
```

This is the **highest-value** hook — every real user request updates the quota for free.

#### 3.3.2 Ping responses (`src/core/ping.js`)

Our pings already issue a tiny chat completion; the response headers are currently discarded. Capture them:

```js
const res = await fetch(...);
processResponseHeaders(providerKey, res.headers);
```

This **pre-warms** the quota display before the user ever routes through the daemon — useful for the CLI-only flow where the daemon isn't running.

#### 3.3.3 Active fetcher merge

`getQuota(providerKey)` returns the **freshest** signal:

```js
function getQuota(providerKey) {
  const passive = _passiveQuota.get(providerKey);
  const active  = lastActiveFetch.get(providerKey); // existing
  const candidates = [passive, active].filter(Boolean);
  if (candidates.length === 0) return null;
  return candidates.reduce((a, b) => a.lastUpdated > b.lastUpdated ? a : b);
}
```

### 3.4 Staleness & display

- A passive snapshot is **stale after 5 min** with no new header (mirror pi-free).
- TUI footer gains a per-provider chip when the daemon is running: `📊 groq 78% · sambanova 41%`.
- Web Dashboard `/stats` returns `quota: { groq: {remaining, limit, percent, lastUpdated, source}, ... }`.

### 3.5 Source attribution (debugging)

Each snapshot stores `source` (which header variant matched). Surface in `--debug` mode so we can see *why* a provider shows 100% (maybe a proxy strips headers → source = `null` → fall back to active fetch).

---

## 4. Subtasks

- [ ] **4.1** Refactor `src/core/provider-quota-fetchers.js`: add `extractQuota`, `processResponseHeaders`, `_passiveQuota` Map, `getQuota` (merge), `getAllQuotas`, `formatQuotaStatus`, staleness constants.
- [ ] **4.2** Unit tests `test/provider-quota-fetchers.test.js` (extend existing):
  - All 6 header pairs parse correctly (one test each).
  - Case-insensitivity (uppercase, mixed-case keys).
  - First-pair-wins priority (when multiple present, the higher-priority one is used).
  - Garbage values (`remaining: "abc"`) → returns null.
  - `limit === 0` → returns null (avoid div-by-zero).
  - Merge: passive newer than active → passive wins, and vice versa.
  - Staleness: snapshot older than 5 min → `formatQuotaStatus` returns undefined.
- [ ] **4.3** Wire `processResponseHeaders` into `src/core/router-daemon.js`'s reverse-proxy response path.
- [ ] **4.4** Wire `processResponseHeaders` into `src/core/ping.js` (capture `res.headers` on every ping).
- [ ] **4.5** `/stats` endpoint: add `quota` object with all providers.
- [ ] **4.6** TUI footer (`src/tui/render-helpers.js`): show top-N provider quota chips when daemon is active.
- [ ] **4.7** Web Dashboard (`web/src/`): render quota bars on the dashboard; subscribe to `/stream/events` for live updates.
- [ ] **4.8** Telemetry: `quota_header_parsed` (with `source` field) — sampled 1/100 to avoid spam.
- [x] **4.9** Docs: update `docs/` quota section, README mention of "live quota, zero extra requests".
  report: README.md updated with a new '📊 Live quota from response headers' section covering: 8-variant header list, where it surfaces (TUI footer / Web Dashboard / /stats.quota), staleness rules, garbage safety, and the full /stats.quota JSON shape. Plus a one-line bullet in the ✨ Features list.
- [x] **4.10** Changelog entry.
  report: Created changelog/v0.5.59.md with full release notes covering: the 8-variant passive parser (with provenance), staleness/merge behaviour, TUI footer chip + Web Dashboard section + /stats.quota exposure, integration into daemon reverse proxy + ping responses, +37 unit tests (632→671 passing), files touched, and the inspiration credit to apmantza/pi-free's quota-monitor.

---

## 5. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After one real routed request to Groq, the TUI shows Groq's `%` within 1s without any extra fetch.
- [ ] After a ping, the quota for that provider is pre-warmed (visible in CLI even without daemon).
- [ ] Providers that don't emit headers still work via the active fetcher fallback.
- [ ] `pnpm test` green (target ≥68 tests after extension).
- [ ] Daemon log shows `quota source=x-ratelimit-remaining` in debug mode.
- [ ] No measurable increase in request count vs baseline (verify by counting pings + routed requests before/after).

---

## 6. Risks & mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Provider strips headers behind a proxy | `source` field reveals it; fall back to active fetch silently. |
| Headers report per-minute but user thinks it's daily | Store which variant matched; show "min" vs "day" in the tooltip if the pair ends in `-day`. |
| Memory growth from old entries | Cap `_passiveQuota` to known providers; evict on provider removal. |
| Race: two routed requests update same provider concurrently | Map writes are atomic in JS (single-threaded event loop); no lock needed. |

---

## 7. References

- pi-free `lib/quota-monitor.ts` — the canonical 6-pair implementation + staleness.
- Our `src/core/provider-quota-fetchers.js` — existing active fetchers (extend, don't replace).
- Our `src/core/router-daemon.js` — reverse-proxy hook point.
- Our `src/core/ping.js` — ping-response hook point.
- Our `test/provider-quota-fetchers.test.js` — extend with the new tests.

## 1. Why

Today every `pnpm start` / `free-coding-models` invocation re-pings **all ~238 models from scratch**, even models that were healthy 5 minutes ago. This is:

- **Wasteful** of free-tier quota on providers that bill per-request even for tiny pings (SambaNova, Groq daily windows, Cerebras before 2026-08-17 shutdown).
- **Not persistent** — a model that has been `broken` for 3 days shows up green again on every fresh launch until its first ping of the day times out.

**Freshness rules** (mirror pi-free exactly):
1. No entry → due for probe.
2. `probeVersion !== CURRENT_PROBE_VERSION` → due for probe (silently re-probed, entry overwritten).
3. `status === 'broken'` → **always due** (allows recovery detection).
4. `now - lastProbedAt >= ttlMs` → due for probe.
5. Otherwise → fresh, skip.

Today `ping-loop.js` iterates `MODELS` and fires pings. Change to:

const dueIds = new Set(getModelsDueForProbe(providerKey, modelIdsForProvider));

emit('cached', cachedHealthy.map(/* build result from cache */));

// 2. Ping only the due ones (parallel, same concurrency as today)

// 3. Merge: cached + fresh → final ranked list

**Critical**: cached results MUST be injected into the TUI immediately — otherwise the user sees an empty table for the duration of the live ping. This is the single biggest perceived-speed win.

- **Toggle** (new `B` key, currently free per `tui-state.js`): reveals them.
- Footer hint: `⚡ 12 cached · 🔴 3 broken hidden (press B to show)`.

# Runtime telemetry: real-world success rate, tok/s, recent calls

> **Priority**: P1 — this is our **differentiating angle**: "82% on the benchmark, *but* 38% real-world success rate at 4 tok/s this week". No competitor exposes this honestly.
> **Inspiration**: `apmantza/pi-free` — `lib/telemetry.ts`.
> **Cross-surface**: collected by the daemon (the only surface that proxies real traffic); consumed by CLI TUI, Web, and Tauri.

---

## 1. Why

Our SWE-bench / tier scores are **static and self-reported** by model providers — a model can advertise 82% and still fail half its real requests through a flaky gateway, or stream at 2 tok/s because the free tier is throttled. pi-free hooks Pi's `turn_end` event and persists, per model:

- `totalCalls`, `successCalls`, `errorCalls` → **real success rate**
- `totalLatencyMs`, `avgLatencyMs`, `avgTokensPerSecond` → **real throughput**
- `recentCalls[]` (last 50) → debugging

We already have `src/core/telemetry.js` (used for product analytics — daemon start/stop, failover, etc.) **but it does not track per-model runtime performance**. This task adds a **second** telemetry stream — *runtime model telemetry* — that becomes a first-class ranking signal and a public "honesty" differentiator.

**Strategic framing**: this turns FCM from "shows you marketing benchmarks" into "shows you what *actually* works on free tiers right now". That's a story no other tool tells.

---

## 2. Goals / Non-goals

### Goals
- [ ] Capture per-model runtime metrics on every routed request through the daemon.
- [ ] Persist to a dedicated JSON file (separate from product telemetry, which is sent upstream).
- [ ] Expose a **real-world score** alongside SWE-bench in the TUI (new sort key, new column).
- [ ] Provide a "Model runtime report" TUI screen (per-model breakdown + recent calls).
- [ ] Privacy: **local-only by default**, opt-in to share (future aggregate leaderboard).

### Non-goals
- Streaming token extraction for partial responses (the PRD already lists this as a known gap; out of scope here).
- Sharing/leaderboard (future task once we have data).
- Collecting prompt/response content (we store metadata only: success, latency, tokens, error).

---

## 3. Technical design

### 3.1 File location

```
~/.free-coding-models/runtime-telemetry.json
```

Separate from product telemetry. Atomic write (reuse the helper from t1). Bounded size (see 3.5).

### 3.2 Schema (mirror pi-free, adapt to our model shape)

```jsonc
{
  "version": 1,
  "models": {
    "nvidiaNim/z-ai/glm-5.2": {
      "totalCalls": 142,
      "successCalls": 131,
      "errorCalls": 11,
      "totalTokens": 184320,
      "totalPromptTokens": 162000,
      "totalCompletionTokens": 22320,
      "totalLatencyMs": 874300,
      "totalCost": 0,                 // free tier
      "recentCalls": [
        {
          "timestamp": 1753478400000,
          "provider": "nvidiaNim",
          "model": "z-ai/glm-5.2",
          "success": true,
          "latencyMs": 1840,
          "promptTokens": 1200,
          "completionTokens": 340,
          "totalTokens": 1540,
          "tokensPerSecond": 184.7,
          "stopReason": "stop",
          "error": null
        }
        // ... capped at 50
      ],
      "lastUpdated": 1753478400000
    }
  },
  "lastUpdated": 1753478400000
}
```

**Derived on read** (don't persist, recompute):
```js
avgLatencyMs       = totalLatencyMs / totalCalls;
avgTokensPerSecond = totalCompletionTokens / (totalLatencyMs / 1000);
successRate        = successCalls / totalCalls;
```

Add a parallel set of functions (do **not** mix with the existing product-telemetry API — different file, different concerns):

  // callResult: { success, latencyMs, promptTokens, completionTokens, stopReason, error }
  // updates in-memory store, computes tokensPerSecond, appends to recentCalls (cap 50)
  // schedules async flush

export function getRealWorldScore(providerKey, modelId) {
  // returns 0..100 composite used for ranking:
  //   score = successRate * 60 + speedScore(avgTok/s) * 25 + recencyBonus * 15
  //   (weights TBD with Vanessa; see 3.6)

### 3.4 Hook point: daemon reverse proxy

The daemon already tracks token usage for the `/stats/tokens` endpoint (per PRD: "Non-streaming OpenAI `usage` fields are tracked daily/all-time"). Extend that same response handler to also call `recordModelCall`:

```js
// in router-daemon.js, after the upstream response completes:
recordModelCall(providerKey, routedModelId, {
  success: !errored,
  latencyMs: Date.now() - requestStart,
  promptTokens: usage?.prompt_tokens ?? 0,
  completionTokens: usage?.completion_tokens ?? 0,

**For streaming**: capture `usage` from the final SSE chunk (OpenAI sends it when `stream_options.include_usage`). For upstreams that don't, fall back to counting streamed chunks (rough estimate). This is the known gap; do the easy case first.

### 3.5 Bounded size

- `recentCalls` capped at **50** per model (FIFO).
- On flush, prune models with `lastUpdated` older than **30 days** (configurable).

### 3.6 Real-world score (the ranking signal)

Composite score so the TUI can sort by it (new sort key, candidate `W` for "world"/real-world, currently free):

```js
function getRealWorldScore(providerKey, modelId) {
  const t = getModelTelemetry(providerKey, modelId);
  if (!t || t.totalCalls < MIN_CALLS_FOR_SCORE) return null; // not enough data yet

  const successRate = t.successCalls / t.totalCalls;          // 0..1
  const speed       = normalizeSpeed(t.avgTokensPerSecond);    // 0..1 (sigmoid)
  const recency     = recencyDecay(t.lastUpdated);             // 0..1 (1=today, 0=30d ago)

  // Weights — TUNE WITH VANESSA before shipping
  return Math.round((successRate * 0.6 + speed * 0.25 + recency * 0.15) * 100);
}
```

- `MIN_CALLS_FOR_SCORE = 5` — don't show a score until we have signal.
- When `null`, the TUI falls back to SWE-bench (don't punish new models).

- **New sort key** `W`: sorts by real-world score descending.
- **New screen** (`Shift+W`? coordinate with t1's `B` and existing `Shift+R/S/T`): "Runtime Report" — pick a model, see success rate, avg latency, avg tok/s, error breakdown (top errors), recent calls list.

In README + dashboard, frame this as:

This is genuinely novel — no other free-model picker exposes this.

# Passive quota monitoring via response headers

> **Priority**: P1 — eliminates wasted quota-fetch requests and keeps quota *live* during real usage.
> **Inspiration**: `apmantza/pi-free` — `lib/quota-monitor.ts` (which itself credits us: *"Inspired by free-coding-models' extractQuotaPercent"*).
> **Cross-surface**: shared `src/core/provider-quota-fetchers.js` is consumed by CLI, daemon, and Tauri.

---

## 1. Why

Today we discover a provider's remaining quota by **actively fetching** a dedicated quota endpoint (see `src/core/provider-quota-fetchers.js` + `test/provider-quota-fetchers.test.js`). Problems:

- **Extra requests** that consume the very quota we're trying to measure (SambaNova per-minute windows, Groq daily caps).
- **Not all providers expose a quota endpoint** — for those we currently show nothing.
- **Stale between polls** — the daemon polls every N seconds; between polls the displayed `%` is wrong, so users get rate-limited mid-request.

pi-free's insight: **every chat-completion response already carries rate-limit headers**. By hooking the response pipeline (they use Pi's `after_provider_response` event) and parsing 5 header variants in priority order, they get a *free, always-fresh* quota signal with **zero extra requests**.

We should do the same on **two** of our surfaces:

1. **Daemon reverse-proxy** (`src/core/router-daemon.js`) — every routed request's response passes through us; we parse the headers there.
2. **Ping responses** (`src/core/ping.js`) — even health-check pings return headers; we can pre-warm quota before the user ever routes.

The active `provider-quota-fetchers.js` stays as a **fallback** for providers that don't emit headers (e.g. some that need an explicit `/usage` call).

---

## 2. Goals / Non-goals

### Goals
- [ ] Parse rate-limit headers from **every** response that flows through the daemon and through pings.
- [ ] Support the 5 header-pair variants pi-free supports (see 3.2) **plus** any we already handle.
- [ ] Merge with existing active-fetch quota so the displayed value is the freshest of the two.
- [ ] Mark quota as **stale after 5 min** (no header seen recently → fall back to active fetch or hide the chip).
- [ ] Expose via `/stats` and the TUI footer so the user sees live `%` per provider.
- [ ] Zero extra network requests compared to today.

### Non-goals
- Replacing `provider-quota-fetchers.js` entirely (keep as fallback).
- Per-model quota (we track per-provider, since headers are per-provider-key).
- Quota-based auto-routing decisions (separate task; this is observability only).

---

## 3. Technical design

### 3.1 Module: extend `src/core/provider-quota-fetchers.js`

Add a passive tracker alongside the existing active fetchers:

```js
// in-memory quota state (mirrors pi-free's _quotaState Map)
const _passiveQuota = new Map(); // providerKey -> QuotaSnapshot

export function processResponseHeaders(providerKey, headers) {
  const extracted = extractQuota(headers);
  if (!extracted) return;
  _passiveQuota.set(providerKey, { ...extracted, percent, lastUpdated: Date.now() });
}

export function getQuota(providerKey) { /* merge passive + active, return freshest */ }
export function getAllQuotas() { /* ReadonlyMap for /stats */ }
export function formatQuotaStatus(providerKey) { /* "⚠️ groq: 12/100 (12%)" */ }
```

### 3.2 Header-pair variants (priority order)

Straight from pi-free's `HEADER_PAIRS`, each pair is `[remaining, limit]`:

```js
const HEADER_PAIRS = [
  // Per-minute (most common)
  ['x-ratelimit-remaining-requests', 'x-ratelimit-limit-requests'], // SambaNova
  ['x-ratelimit-remaining',          'x-ratelimit-limit'],          // Mistral
  ['ratelimit-remaining-requests',   'ratelimit-limit-requests'],
  ['ratelimit-remaining',            'ratelimit-limit'],
  // Per-day
  ['x-ratelimit-remaining-requests-day', 'x-ratelimit-limit-requests-day'], // SambaNova daily
  ['x-ratelimit-remaining-day',          'x-ratelimit-limit-day'],
];
```

**Case-insensitive**: normalize all header keys to lowercase before matching (some proxies vary casing). Return the **first** pair where both `remaining` and `limit` parse as finite numbers and `limit > 0`.

### 3.3 Integration points

#### 3.3.1 Daemon reverse proxy (`src/core/router-daemon.js`)

The daemon already proxies `/v1/chat/completions`. In the response handler (after we forward headers, before we stream the body to the client), call:

```js
processResponseHeaders(upstreamProviderKey, upstreamResponse.headers);
```

This is the **highest-value** hook — every real user request updates the quota for free.

#### 3.3.2 Ping responses (`src/core/ping.js`)

Our pings already issue a tiny chat completion; the response headers are currently discarded. Capture them:

```js
const res = await fetch(...);
processResponseHeaders(providerKey, res.headers);
```

This **pre-warms** the quota display before the user ever routes through the daemon — useful for the CLI-only flow where the daemon isn't running.

#### 3.3.3 Active fetcher merge

`getQuota(providerKey)` returns the **freshest** signal:

```js
function getQuota(providerKey) {
  const passive = _passiveQuota.get(providerKey);
  const active  = lastActiveFetch.get(providerKey); // existing
  const candidates = [passive, active].filter(Boolean);
  if (candidates.length === 0) return null;
  return candidates.reduce((a, b) => a.lastUpdated > b.lastUpdated ? a : b);
}
```

### 3.4 Staleness & display

- A passive snapshot is **stale after 5 min** with no new header (mirror pi-free).
- TUI footer gains a per-provider chip when the daemon is running: `📊 groq 78% · sambanova 41%`.
- Web Dashboard `/stats` returns `quota: { groq: {remaining, limit, percent, lastUpdated, source}, ... }`.

### 3.5 Source attribution (debugging)

Each snapshot stores `source` (which header variant matched). Surface in `--debug` mode so we can see *why* a provider shows 100% (maybe a proxy strips headers → source = `null` → fall back to active fetch).

---

## 4. Subtasks

- [ ] **4.1** Refactor `src/core/provider-quota-fetchers.js`: add `extractQuota`, `processResponseHeaders`, `_passiveQuota` Map, `getQuota` (merge), `getAllQuotas`, `formatQuotaStatus`, staleness constants.
- [ ] **4.2** Unit tests `test/provider-quota-fetchers.test.js` (extend existing):
  - All 6 header pairs parse correctly (one test each).
  - Case-insensitivity (uppercase, mixed-case keys).
  - First-pair-wins priority (when multiple present, the higher-priority one is used).
  - Garbage values (`remaining: "abc"`) → returns null.
  - `limit === 0` → returns null (avoid div-by-zero).
  - Merge: passive newer than active → passive wins, and vice versa.
  - Staleness: snapshot older than 5 min → `formatQuotaStatus` returns undefined.
- [ ] **4.3** Wire `processResponseHeaders` into `src/core/router-daemon.js`'s reverse-proxy response path.
- [ ] **4.4** Wire `processResponseHeaders` into `src/core/ping.js` (capture `res.headers` on every ping).
- [ ] **4.5** `/stats` endpoint: add `quota` object with all providers.
- [ ] **4.6** TUI footer (`src/tui/render-helpers.js`): show top-N provider quota chips when daemon is active.
- [ ] **4.7** Web Dashboard (`web/src/`): render quota bars on the dashboard; subscribe to `/stream/events` for live updates.
- [ ] **4.8** Telemetry: `quota_header_parsed` (with `source` field) — sampled 1/100 to avoid spam.
- [ ] **4.9** Docs: update `docs/` quota section, README mention of "live quota, zero extra requests".
- [ ] **4.10** Changelog entry.

---

## 5. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After one real routed request to Groq, the TUI shows Groq's `%` within 1s without any extra fetch.
- [ ] After a ping, the quota for that provider is pre-warmed (visible in CLI even without daemon).
- [ ] Providers that don't emit headers still work via the active fetcher fallback.
- [ ] `pnpm test` green (target ≥68 tests after extension).
- [ ] Daemon log shows `quota source=x-ratelimit-remaining` in debug mode.
- [ ] No measurable increase in request count vs baseline (verify by counting pings + routed requests before/after).

---

## 6. Risks & mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Provider strips headers behind a proxy | `source` field reveals it; fall back to active fetch silently. |
| Headers report per-minute but user thinks it's daily | Store which variant matched; show "min" vs "day" in the tooltip if the pair ends in `-day`. |
| Memory growth from old entries | Cap `_passiveQuota` to known providers; evict on provider removal. |
| Race: two routed requests update same provider concurrently | Map writes are atomic in JS (single-threaded event loop); no lock needed. |

---

## 7. References

- pi-free `lib/quota-monitor.ts` — the canonical 6-pair implementation + staleness.
- Our `src/core/provider-quota-fetchers.js` — existing active fetchers (extend, don't replace).
- Our `src/core/router-daemon.js` — reverse-proxy hook point.
- Our `src/core/ping.js` — ping-response hook point.
- Our `test/provider-quota-fetchers.test.js` — extend with the new tests.
